methods.label: Connect the angles through their sines
methods.explanation:
The useful angle relation is \(36^\circ+72^\circ=108^\circ=180^\circ-72^\circ\). It lets the sine addition formula connect the two desired cosines.

Write \(c=\cos36^\circ\) and \(d=\cos72^\circ\). Since supplementary angles have equal sines,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin72^\circ
&=\sin(72^\circ+36^\circ)\\
&=\sin72^\circ\,c+d\sin36^\circ.
\end{aligned}
\]
The sine addition formula also gives \(\sin72^\circ=2\sin36^\circ\,c\). Substituting this into the preceding equation yields
\[
2\sin36^\circ\,c
=\sin36^\circ(2c^2+d).
\]
Because \(\sin36^\circ>0\), division by it is valid, giving \(2c=2c^2+d\). The cosine double-angle formula says \(d=2c^2-1\), so
\[
2c=(d+1)+d,
\qquad c-d=\frac12.
\]
Therefore \(x=\boxed{\frac12}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
